page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a low-memory, compute-dense virtual machine architecture from the Dlsv7 family. It is equipped with 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. The system provides 96.0 GB of memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation, coupled with an extensive 480 MB L3 cache. Vector extensions and hardware acceleration are available through AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include local disk storage or bundled public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark evaluations reveal substantial computational and instruction-level performance. The configuration scores in the upper tier across PassMark CPU metrics, achieving 66,066.16 in overall CPU capacity alongside strong results in extended instructions, cryptographic operations, and physics simulations. Compression throughput is similarly elevated, delivering 36.1 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 303.78 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In application-tier tests, the server demonstrated 79.02 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks, 75.36 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and upper-quartile token processing on small-to-medium size language models.

While execution throughput and integer computation are robust, overall memory capacity represents a structural constraint. With only 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, memory footprint limits tasks that require massive in-memory datasets or deep buffering. Stress-ng scores and uncached memory bandwidth fall within average performance tiers compared to peer server profiles. Cost efficiency is driven by the reduced memory-to-vCPU ratio, minimizing resource waste in compute-heavy scenarios that do not demand extensive RAM capacity.

This server type is suitable for compute-intensive workloads that operate within lean memory boundaries. Target applications include microservices orchestration, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch compression tasks, web servers handling high connection rates, network edge proxies, and targeted CPU-based inferencing.

The system provides 96.0 GB of RAM, allocating 2.0 GB per vCPU, along with a 480 MB L3 cache and support for AMX and AVX-512 instructions. Local storage is not provided, necessitating external block storage for persistent state. Benchmark metrics show top-tier execution across PassMark CPU tests, Redis operations reaching 79.02 million ops/sec, and high-throughput static web serving at 75.36 GB/sec. Due to its reduced memory footprint, this instance is efficient for CPU-heavy deployments that do not require high memory-per-core ratios, such as batch compression, web frontends, and API routing.
